title: Intrinsic String Manipulation Types knowledge check

questions.prompt: What can a template literal type express?
options: A string pattern assembled from literal types and unions at compile time.
A regular expression that runs automatically on each string.
A string that is encrypted at runtime.
questions.answer_key: A string pattern assembled from literal types and unions at compile time.
questions.explanation: Template literal types constrain string shapes statically; runtime validation remains separate.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Intrinsic String Manipulation Types”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with uppercase and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with uppercase and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Uppercase”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Intrinsic String Manipulation Types”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check lowercase, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume capitalize and uncapitalize is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check lowercase, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Lowercase”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
